title: Raspberry fudge
subtitle: creamy condensed milk fudge with a sharp raspberry note
excerpt: Raspberry fudge uses condensed milk as the base, beaten with icing sugar and butter off the heat, with raspberry jam stirred through at the end for a sharp fruity flavour through the sweet, creamy fudge. The jam goes in last to keep the raspberry flavour fresh and bright. The mixture sets in the fridge rather than at room temperature, giving a soft, creamy result.
sourceNotes: Condensed milk fudge method documented in British confectionery books from the mid-twentieth century. Fruit jam as a flavouring in no-cook condensed milk fudge is a common British home-baking adaptation.

recipe.freezeNotes: Wrap individual pieces in waxed paper and freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Remove from the fridge 15 minutes before serving.

content.text: Raspberry fudge is a condensed milk fudge made without a sugar thermometer. The base is heated on the hob, removed from the heat, beaten with icing sugar until thick, and raspberry jam is stirred through at the end. The result is a soft, creamy fudge with a sharp fruity note through it. It sets in the fridge.
Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper, leaving an overhang on two sides so you can lift the fudge out cleanly.
Put the condensed milk and butter into a medium saucepan over a low heat. Stir until the butter melts and the mixture is smooth and warm. Do not let it boil.

Remove from the heat. Add the sifted icing sugar and vanilla extract. Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon or silicone spatula for 2 to 3 minutes until very thick and fudgy. The mixture will pull away from the sides of the pan.
Add the raspberry jam and stir briefly until just swirled through. Do not over-mix; a few streaks of jam look better than a fully blended pale pink.
Pour into the lined tin and press into an even layer with the back of a spoon. Leave to cool for 20 minutes at room temperature, then chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Lift out using the baking paper overhang and cut into squares with a sharp, warm knife.

attrs.problem: Fudge too soft and not setting firmly
attrs.avoid: Avoid under-beating; if the icing sugar is not fully beaten in, the fudge stays loose and does not set.
attrs.fix: Beat for a further 2 minutes on the hob over the lowest possible heat, stirring constantly until the mixture thickens more noticeably.

attrs.problem: Jam sinking to the bottom rather than swirling through
attrs.avoid: Avoid adding the jam to the mixture while it is still very warm and liquid; it will sink to the bottom.
attrs.fix: Allow the fudge to cool and thicken for 5 minutes before adding the jam, then stir through with only 3 or 4 turns of the spatula.
